root_cause: The tab navigation does not skip disabled tabs when moving with arrow keys, causing focus and activation to land on a disabled tab.
repair_strategy: Modify the _keydown method in the Tab class to skip disabled tabs by repeatedly calling getNextActiveElement until an enabled tab is found, using the isDisabled utility.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight will move focus to the next enabled tab (Billing) and activate it, complying with keyboard navigation expectations for a tablist.
functional_risks: Potential infinite loop if all tabs are disabled (mitigated by assuming at least one enabled).
Change may affect behavior if downstream code relies on activating disabled tabs via keyboard (unlikely).
Ensure that the disabled tab remains non-focusable and not activatable via arrow keys.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowRight from the first tab skips the disabled second tab and focuses/activates the third tab.
Verify that aria-selected becomes true on the third tab and false on others.
Verify that the disabled tab remains with aria-selected false and not focusable.
Verify that ArrowLeft wraps correctly from the first tab to the last enabled tab.
Verify that other keyboard interactions (click, programmatic show) still work as expected.
